problem: Which of the following gives the line integral of the function $f(x,y)=x+{y}^{2},$ traversed once along the circle $C$ with equation ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=4?$
worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}s={\int }_{a}^{b}f(r(t))\,‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t.
$$

 

The curve $C$ is a circle of radius $2$ centered at $O.$ It can be parametrized as 

$$
r(t)=⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,\,0\le t<2\pi .
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)j \\  & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{sin}^{2}⁡t+4{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\sqrt{4({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y)=x+{y}^{2},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡t+(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2} \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡t+4{sin}^{2}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }f(r(t))\,‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t+4{sin}^{2}⁡t)\cdot 2\cdot \text{d}t \\  & =4{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+2{sin}^{2}⁡t)\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$
